rows.grounds: locative singular masculine/neuter adjective used adverbially for the right side
compound kara+daṇḍa in accusative singular neuter; fused form kept as one token
locative singular masculine/neuter adjective used for the left side
fused sandhi form of ca+eva with final ā retained before bhayaṃkare; not expanded
locative singular masculine/neuter adjective describing the left-hand object or hand

items.question: Which implements are held in the deity's right and left hands?
premises: The right hand holds a staff.
The left hand holds a fear-causing implement.
items.inference: The described iconographic form carries a staff in the right hand and a fear-causing object in the left hand.
uncertainties: The fused token caivā is not expanded into its internal sandhi parts.
The noun for the left-hand object is implied rather than explicitly named.
items.plain_english: In the right hand, indeed, a staff; in the left, indeed, a fear-causing implement.
